notes.raw:
Heat capacity (cal/mol·K) and enthalpy (kcal/mol) equations: 
298.15-3000 K: $Cp^{0} = 7.990 + 0.476 \times 10^{-3} T - 0.898 \times 10^{5} T^{-2}$ $H^{0} - H_{298}^{0} = 7.990 \times 10^{-3} T + 0.238 \times 10^{-6} T^{2} + 0.898 \times 10^{2} T^{-1} - 2.705$ 
Reaction equations (kcal/mol): 
298.15-2000 K: $\Delta Hr^{\circ} = 53.508 + 0.301 \times 10^{-3} T - 0.688 \times 10^{-6} T^{2} - 116.650 T^{-1}$ $\Delta Gr^{\circ} = 53.508 - 0.301 \times 10^{-3} T \ln T + 0.688 \times 10^{-6} T^{2} - 58.325 T^{-1} - 20.729 \times 10^{-3} T$ 2000-3000 K: $\Delta Hr^{\circ} = 56.525 - 2.406 \times 10^{-3} T + 0.054 \times 10^{-6} T^{2} - 1260.200 T^{-1}$ $\Delta Gr^{\circ} = 56.525 + 2.406 \times 10^{-3} T \ln T - 0.054 \times 10^{-6} T^{2} - 630.100 T^{-1} - 41.182 \times 10^{-3} T$ 
Sources: Enthalpy of formation at 298 K based on Bell (7) and Fincham (40). Other data based on Hildenbrand (53) and Lagerqvist (71).
